title: Zelensky Says Ukraine Will Resume Russian Refinery Strikes, Defying Trump
partialText: President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed overt frustration with the United States in an interview with The Financial Times. He had paused the strikes to comply with a demand from the United States.

title: Why Russia Sees a Window to Bomb Ukraine Into Submission This Winter
partialText: Moscow is not winning on the battlefield. Instead, it is seizing an opening to inflict immense human suffering in Ukrainian cities.

title: Data Centers Become Targets in Wars in Ukraine, Russia and the Middle East
partialText: Military forces have sought to damage the computing hubs that power online services and artificial intelligence systems.

title: Trump Cancels Planned Execution Livestream of Nidal Hasan, Fort Hood Shooter
partialText: The president said only immediate families of the victims of the mass shooting in 2009 would witness the execution of Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan.

title: Homeownership Drifts Further Out of Reach as Mortgage Rates Rise
partialText: Mortgage rates have pushed above 7 percent and home prices remain elevated, hurting the prospects of would-be buyers.

title: California’s Proposition 45 Brings the Sprawl Debate Back
partialText: Among the measures up for a vote in November is one that would amend the state’s landmark environmental law and make it easier to build large housing developments outside cities.

title: Mortgage Rates Hover at 7.4%, Highest Since 2023
partialText: The average 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage has steadily risen in recent weeks, compounding affordability challenges for many Americans.

title: Why Does Saudi Arabia Struggle to Stop Houthi Attacks?
partialText: The Saudi military has expensive equipment, but the missiles and drones used by the Yemeni militia are difficult to detect and stop.

title: Iran-Backed Houthis Strike Presidential Palace, Yemen Says
partialText: Two were killed when Houthi missiles struck the Maashiq Presidential Palace in Aden, a Yemeni minister said. Saudi Arabia has said Iran is fueling the country’s escalating conflict.

title: Is the Fox Collie the Perfect Dog for Our Aimless Era?
partialText: A winemaker in Northern California is convinced that a dog once bred to herd sheep in the Scottish Highlands is the ideal pet for our uncertain times.

title: The Image of the Great Flood That Stuck With Me: Caskets Floating Away
partialText: Isabel Wilkerson remembers covering a flood powerful enough to disrupt the dead.

title: Democrats Worry About Tight Midterm Races in Maine, Michigan and Minnesota
partialText: Despite hopes for a blue wave, Democratic candidates in Minnesota, Maine and Michigan are facing local political headwinds and have struggled to open up clear daylight in the polls.

title: Trump’s Attacks on Voting Raise Fears He Will Try to Challenge Midterm Results
partialText: Election officials say they worry the administration could use its own unsubstantiated claims to contest the vote in November.

title: As Texas Schools Add Police Officers to Campuses, Some Students Are Facing Serious Charges
partialText: More students ages 10 to 13 are ending up in the justice system after vaping, making threats and lashing out at school.

title: Para ciertos estudiantes en Texas, una leve falta puede derivar en cargos penales
partialText: Una investigación muestra cómo niños de entre 10 y 13 años son remitidos al sistema legal por exabruptos comunes de su edad, o infracciones como vapear, que no representan una amenaza grave real.

title: Mamdani Taps His Social Media Charm on Behalf of Hochul, a Crucial Ally
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s first campaign video for Gov. Kathy Hochul, in which he attacks her Republican rival, Bruce Blakeman, has some of the mayor’s hallmark appeal, but a bit less pizazz.

title: Anti-Israel Protesters Pose a Purity Test That Even Mamdani Can’t Pass
partialText: The enmity directed toward Mayor Zohran Mamdani from within the pro-Palestinian movement illustrates the challenge the wider left faces in corralling its insurgents.

title: 7 Years Old, No Lawyer: Migrant Children Face Deportation Hearings Alone
partialText: For years, the government has helped secure lawyers for minors who arrive at the southern border. But a contract dispute has forced many children to face immigration judges on their own.

title: Trump’s Democracy-for-Diesel Deal Shames Us All
partialText: The president’s arrangement to import Russian diesel fuel is one more example of how he has sold out American democracy.

partialText: Dwarkesh Patel on what the public doesn’t know about A.I.

title: Harvard Endowment Soars to $68 Billion Even as Federal Cuts Force Layoffs
partialText: The stock market has boosted Harvard’s wealth. But as federal funding slumps, the school is seeking corporate sponsors to underwrite research.
